note: Guards issue #57. The `File` path helpers called `to_s` on their path argument, so a non-String path answered a string where CRuby raises `TypeError` — `File.dirname(123)` was `"."` and `File.basename(123)` was `"123"`, a wrong answer rather than a decline. Every path argument now goes through `File.__path_str`, a model of `rb_get_path`: String as itself, `to_path` next (through `method_missing`, so the callability test is the `rb_check_funcall` one), then `StringValue` on whatever it answered, and an object with no `to_path` goes to `StringValue` itself — hence `dirname-bad_path` names Integer and `dirname-bad_str` names the receiver and the method it came from. `File.basename`'s suffix is a plain `StringValue` (no `to_path`), converted before the path as CRuby orders them, and an explicit nil suffix is refused rather than read as absent. `File.join` modelled along with it, because flattening and the conversion are the same question: nested Arrays are spliced, a self-referential one is `ArgumentError: recursive array` by object identity (`rb_exec_recursive`), and the boundary is not `join("/")` — a trailing separator run on the left is dropped when the right side starts with one, and an empty left side still contributes a separator, which is why `File.join([], "a")` is `"/a"`. Not covered here: `File.dirname`'s optional level argument (the model still rejects it) and the path-arithmetic disagreements on trailing and repeated separators — separate issues.
